summary: In ansible-core 2.13, fetch_url returns the captured HTTPError as the response object, so modules should check info['status'] >= 400 to detect failures rather than r being None.
questions: fetch_url no longer returns None on HTTP errors, how do I detect a failure?
How can my module read the body of a 404 response from fetch_url?

answer_card.title: fetch_url returns HTTPError responses
answer_card.answer_md:
`fetch_url` now returns the **`HTTPError`** as `r` (a response-like object you can `.read()`). Detect failures by status:

```python
r, info = fetch_url(module, url)
if info['status'] >= 400:
    module.fail_json(msg='HTTP error', status=info['status'], body=r.read() if r else None)
```

Don't rely on `r is None` or catching `AttributeError`.
